raw_response:
I did not find a verified, ready-made library that meets the complete request: a function callable from JavaScript that takes the Bash associative-array source string, produces the settings-value object, and is licensed with its library under AGPL3.

The only AGPL-specific lead I found was [@themoltnet/shell-command-analyzer](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@themoltnet/shell-command-analyzer). Its public search listing describes a JavaScript package built around a Bash parser and claims AGPL-3.0-only. However, my attempts to open the package and its README failed. The visible description concerns command/argument security analysis, and I could not verify any function that extracts associative-array values into your desired object. I would keep this only as an unresolved lead, with low confidence in its usefulness for your purpose. The indexed release also appears later than July 3, 2026, so it is not evidence of an available answer on that date.

The nearby libraries I could inspect have specific mismatches:

- [bash-parser](https://github.com/vorpaljs/bash-parser) documents a JavaScript parse function returning an abstract syntax tree and explicitly uses the MIT license. It therefore does not meet the stated AGPL3 license requirement. The README also does not establish a ready-made array-to-value-object function.
- [unbash](https://github.com/webpro-nl/unbash) documents Bash parsing and a JavaScript/TypeScript AST visitor. The repository identifies ISC licensing. Extracting literal assignment values would require additional work, and the examined current package material is not historical July evidence.
- [mvdan/sh](https://github.com/mvdan/sh) documents a Go parser/interpreter under BSD-3-Clause. Its shfmt JSON mode represents the syntax tree. The interface I inspected is a Go library/command-line program, so it does not supply the requested AGPL3 JavaScript function.
- [json.bash](https://github.com/h4l/json.bash) documents JSON generation from a Bash API and command-line tools. This could serve a shell-side export design, but the documented interface does not accept a Bash source string through the JavaScript library API you described. I did not verify its license.

For any future candidate, the decisive verification is an accessible, versioned example or function that consumes your two-step declaration/assignment, handles the shown quotes and line continuations, and returns the actual version-to-address values. A parser returning an AST leaves that value-mapping step to application code. Your sample also changes contract_address to contract-address; that should be treated as an explicit output-key choice rather than inferred as a general renaming rule.

I have linked the existing projects and have not reproduced their implementations. This result is documentation-based; no package was installed or executed. It reports an unsuccessful bounded search for a complete match, not proof that no such library exists.
